entities.summary:
The Technical University of Munich (TUM), established in 1868, stands as a premier public research university located in Munich, Germany. It plays a pivotal role in shaping higher education and research in Europe, especially in the fields of engineering, natural sciences, and applied sciences. TUM's founding was driven by the need to advance technical education during the industrial revolution, with influential figures such as its first president, Johann von Thiersch, guiding its vision and development.

From its inception, TUM has made significant strides in education and innovation. The university was one of the first in Germany to adopt a modern research-oriented curriculum, which led to groundbreaking achievements, such as the development of the first German aircraft engines and contributions to quantum mechanics by notable scholars like Werner Heisenberg. With over 18,000 students enrolled and a faculty of distinguished researchers, TUM has fostered a collaborative environment that encourages innovation and entrepreneurship, evident in its numerous successful spin-offs and partnerships with industries.

The legacy of TUM is profound, influencing the landscape of higher education in Germany and beyond. It has produced numerous Nobel laureates, including physicist Max Planck and chemist Robert H. Grubbs, who have had far-reaching impacts on science and technology. TUM’s commitment to research and development has established it as a model for other institutions, facilitating international academic collaboration and contributing to the global knowledge economy. The university's motto, 'The Entrepreneurial University,' encapsulates its forward-thinking ethos, preparing students to meet contemporary challenges and drive future innovations.
